newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss guard in shredding case loses job - media.
newsitem.headline: Swiss guard in shredding case loses job - media.

text.p: A guard who rescued documents due to be shredded at a Swiss bank and turned them over to a Jewish group has lost his job with a security firm, Swiss television and a news agency reported on Sunday.
The Swiss news agency SDA quoted a lawyer defending watchman Christoph Meili as saying that he had lost his job with a security firm.
Swiss television reported that Meili's dismissal would be effective in April.
Meili had been suspended after the incident.
Officials of the security firm were not immediaterly contactable to comment on the media reports.
Meili discovered the documents, set to be destroyed, in a shredder room at Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) and without first telling the bank he turned the documents over to a local Jewish group.
The documents pertained to a German bank owned by Union Bank of Switzerland during the period when Nazis were beginning to misappropriate Jewish assets and take businesses away from Jewish owners.

UBS called the incident a "regrettable mistake". It admitted that the shredding was in violation of a government ban adopted in December which prohibits destruction of information that could serve to shed light on Swiss activities during the Nazi era.
